nbis.headline: No new price discovery yet. Fri cash $165.47 (−12.18%) stands; Yahoo overnight $171.52 (+3.66%) at 08:25 ICT, not cash. Cap $44.98B (CNBC). About THB 5,530/sh at 33.42. Still −33.8% from 6 Oct $249.87.
nbis.why: The bounce is under 5% and on thin overnight volume. Futures are up, but Fri FLAG levels still hold.

nbis.headline: EDGAR: no new filing after the Grimme Form 4 (0001513845-26-000130, accepted 17 Oct 00:05Z). No new 6-K since Inferize on 1 Oct.
nbis.why: No dilution, convert or guidance change over the weekend.

nbis.headline: Peer hit: Microsoft withdrew from Nscale's Loughton, Essex data-center lease after grid power was pushed into the 2030s. Nscale says its other Microsoft deals are unaffected. Bloomberg reports IPO investors pushing Nscale's ~$30B valuation down toward $16-19B.
nbis.why: This is a new data point that hyperscaler offtake can be pulled. It feeds the neocloud discount, though it is a power and site problem, not a demand problem, and not Nebius-specific.

nbis.headline: The Information (18 Oct): industry executives expect only 7-10 of hundreds of neoclouds to survive. Nvidia is backing chosen operators with easier credit, site help and about $20B of leases it can reassign.
nbis.why: Scale and balance sheet now decide who survives. Nebius has about $8.0B cash (CNBC) and lower leverage than CoreWeave, which argues it is a survivor, but the group still trades together.

nbis.headline: Nebius newsroom (19 Oct): AI Builder Program in Europe, $10M of compute grants plus Accel/VC and NVIDIA community links.
nbis.why: Marketing. Not material against a $45B market cap.

aiInfra.headline: META reports Q3 after the close Wed 21 Oct (call 4:30 pm ET), not 28 Oct as prior desks had it. Guide: Q3 revenue $61-64B, 2026 capex $130-145B. TSLA, LRCX, TXN, IBM and SAP report the same evening.
aiInfra.why: First hyperscaler capex read lands this week, a week before GOOGL (28 Oct) and AMZN (29 Oct).

aiInfra.headline: SPCX posts Q3 after the close Tue 20 Oct (IR notice 16 Oct). Under the lockup terms Dagom summarizes, up to ~1.3B shares (28% of the lockup group) unlock on the 2nd full trading day after results; by our count that is Thu 22 Oct, before the 328.4M tranche on 24 Oct.
aiInfra.why: The biggest supply step moves into this week. Eligibility is not selling, but Q3 now has to carry the stock into it.

aiInfra.headline: SK hynix live ₩1,248,000 (−1.89%) at 10:27 KST against the KRX Fri close of ₩1,272,000. It opened ₩1,215,000 and hit ₩1,182,000 (−7.1%) before foreign buying cut the loss. Samsung ₩217,750 (+1.04%). Last week SK fell 24.3% and Samsung 17.8%, the worst weeks since 2008.
aiInfra.why: No FLAG on the live print. Korea is absorbing the Fri US tape and the DeepSeek news better than feared.

aiInfra.headline: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 on 17 Oct. It claims to beat leading US models on coding and agent benchmarks at $0.60 per million output tokens off-peak; posts also claim it tops Kimi K3 on one benchmark. FN News flagged it as a new weight on Korean chip stocks.
aiInfra.why: This repeats the January 2025 'cheap model, less capex' fear. Memory and GPU names are most exposed. K3 is still private with no ticker.

aiInfra.headline: Reuters/Seoul Economic Daily (18 Oct): Nvidia asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to make base dies for its custom NVHBM on TSMC 3nm. Samsung agreed, its first use of TSMC for HBM.
aiInfra.why: Nvidia gains more control over HBM design. It is neutral to mildly negative for SK and MU differentiation, with no volume change stated.

aiInfra.headline: US book unchanged at Fri closes: GOOGL $340.59, AMZN $250.00, META $709.33, NVDA $214.13, MU $878.84 (Fri FLAG), SPCX $146.03. GOOGL Q3 28 Oct and AMZN Q3 29 Oct are confirmed by IR. K3 (Moonshot AI) is private with no ticker.
aiInfra.why: No US cash session since Fri.

macro.headline: Sunday-night futures bounced: ES 7,742.25 (+0.49%), NQ 29,682.75 (+0.99%), YM +0.14% (CNBC, 08:15 ICT). 10Y 5.071% (−2.7bp), 2Y 4.719%. Nikkei −1.3%, Taiwan −1.8%, KOSPI −0.1% after opening −3.2%.
macro.why: Dip buying in AI names before a heavy earnings week. Asia is weaker than US futures.

macro.headline: Oil eased: Brent $108.43 (−1.3%), WTI $101.16 (−0.25%), after Trump waived some Russia sanctions; he later said no final decision. Iran reported another tanker hit a mine in Hormuz, and Houthis targeted Saudi Yanbu.
macro.why: Oil above $100 still feeds the inflation path into the FOMC on 27-28 Oct. Lower oil helped bonds overnight.

macro.headline: AI-debt backdrop over the weekend: NYT/Business Times say CoreWeave bonds price a more than 60% chance it misses obligations, and Barclays says AI debt spreads are up over 50% in six months. Oracle and SoftBank credit are also under pressure.
macro.why: Financing risk, not demand, is still driving neocloud valuations.

macro.headline: China Q3 GDP and Sep activity data are due at 10:00 Beijing (09:00 ICT); the Reuters poll expects 4.4% y/y. The Fed is in blackout until the 28 Oct decision. USDTHB 33.42 (open.er-api), DXY 101.85. CNN F&G 17.9 Extreme Fear, unchanged.
macro.why: China data and stimulus talk at the Financial Street Forum are the next Asia catalysts. US data this week is light: housing starts, claims, UMich.
